# Background and related work

**Latent planning.** @hanna2026latent define latent planning as internal
representations that (i)~cause a specific future token or concept
(forward planning) and (ii)~shape preceding context to license it
(backward planning). On \(a\)/\(an\) tasks they report that reliable
behavioral success emerges mainly at larger scales; small models fail
often yet can host nascent mechanisms. Our work does not dispute that
scale story. We ask a sharper local question: when sparse interventions
on a *small* model *do* move articles, do free-generation noun-token
changes identify separable planning, or can they be explained by
mediation through the generated article?

**Feature circuits and steering.** Attribution graphs over sparse
autoencoders / transcoders estimate contributions among features and
logits [@ameisen2025attribution; @lindsey2025biology;
@dunefsky2024transcoders; @marks2025sparse]. We use `circuit-tracer` with
Gemma Scope~2 cross-layer transcoders [@hanna2025circuittracer;
@gemmascope2] to select features and intervene. Affine skip connections
improve reconstruction but allow MLP computation to bypass sparse
features; we therefore also test dense MLP-in interventions, including
an oracle activation-patching positive control.

**Causal mediation in autoregressive models.** Holding an intervening
generated token fixed is a standard way to separate total effects from
paths through that token. Our contribution is to apply this control to
article--noun interventions that are easy to misread as modular planning
under free generation, and to show how floor effects and small samples
limit strong negative claims about latent edges.
